name: facts arrive as symmetric truths; using them requires choosing a direction, and the choice decides whether anything ever finishes
condition: The world delivers facts as equalities between two forms with no indication of which form is preferred. To use a fact the organism must commit to a direction (replace occurrences of one form by the other). Directions are chosen by the organism, persist in its store, and are applied automatically thereafter. Fitness is earned by reaching stable answers within budget across a long stream of problems; the same store is used across the stream, so a bad orientation chosen early costs for the rest of the run.
capability_rewarded: Choosing orientations for a growing set of symmetric facts so that automatic application terminates and reaches answers the world accepts; revising an orientation when evidence shows it was wrong; recognising facts that should be stored in neither direction.
world_requirements: facts delivered unoriented (both sides given, no preference signalled by the world; the presentation order is randomised so that 'left as given' carries no information)
a fact stream in which some facts have an obvious size-reducing direction, some are size-neutral (permutations), some are size-increasing in both directions but useful in one for later facts
problems checkable by the world without the store
a shared long-run store so orientation choices have consequences beyond the current problem
a report per problem of steps used and of whether the budget was exhausted
vacuity_condition: Vacuous if the world's presentation order correlates with the good direction (then 'keep as given' wins and no choice is made -- the randomisation requirement closes this), OR if every fact has a strictly size-reducing direction (then 'pick the smaller side' is a complete policy and the pressure measures nothing). Eligibility: the count of facts in the stream whose better direction is NOT the size-reducing one must be > 0 and reported.
trivial_shortcuts: orient toward the smaller side always (closable by facts whose good direction is size-increasing)
store nothing symmetric (closable: some problems need a permutation fact in one direction)
store both directions (closable: automatic application of both directions loops and the budget catches it)
read the presentation order (closed by randomisation)
cheat_control: Deliver the same fact stream to two copies of the organism with the presentation order of the two sides swapped. If the copies converge to the same orientations and the same scores, the organism is choosing; if their scores differ by more than the noise floor, they are inheriting orientation from presentation and the world is not measuring the capability. Additionally plant one fact whose size-reducing direction is a trap (it enables a loop with an earlier fact) and check that the disciplined organism reverses or drops it after the loop bites. READ-OUT RULE (added 2026-09-11 on Vivarium #182): this is an invariance null and it is ONE-SIDED. Copies that DISAGREE beyond noise prove the organism inherits orientation from presentation (the defect). Copies that AGREE prove only equivariance under the swap -- NOT that any orientation was chosen. Agreement must be followed by the planted-trap check (the size-reducing direction that loops) before the capability is credited; without it the read-out is over-read.
negative_control: A stream of facts each with one strictly size-reducing direction and no interaction: any orientation policy that picks the smaller side scores maximally, and a copy that picks randomly must score lower (so the world CAN distinguish policies at all).
notes: This is the pressure Nyx believes carries most of the ancestor's capability: in the ancestor the direction is chosen by HUMANS at the moment a fact is tagged, encoded as which side was written on the left, and a large community curates the result (48,076 tag sites at the pin). No mechanism in the specimen chooses orientation; the specimen inherits it. If Vivarium finds this pressure operational, the finding is that the famous system's fitness sits mostly in DATA plus POLICY, not in machinery -- one of the prompt's named valid outcomes.
